source_basis.note: Pure computational continuation of the same frozen role-local scheduler question. No production latency calibration introduced.

tested_grid.candidate_policy: same globally-certified b16 frontier witness: five (20,16) audits followed by fifteen (50,36), rho=.20, exact curtailment
tested_grid.reveal: fixed precommitted pair order; hidden higher-index results quarantined; hard deadline => unresolved
tested_grid.capacity_note: Changing b changes peak reserved side slots from 2b; q95 full-obligation occupancy does not price peak reservation.
tested_grid.sampling: Per model/b/action/outcome: 900 fail and 300 commit stage draws. Within a draw the three schedulers and all W values shared N and side latencies. Each scheduler cell used 120000 full-run resamples with exact candidate-level commit probabilities. This grid is a coarse joint screen; the predecessor W128 b16 pair-vs-side comparison used 8000/3000 stage draws and 600000 full-run paired resamples.

conversation_like.fixed_SLO: D = q95 wall of pair-tied b16,W128 = 746.220 normalized units

code_like_plus_straggler.fixed_SLO: D = q95 wall of pair-tied b16,W128 = 4371.673 normalized units

key_results.pooling_check: Across all 18 matched b/W/model cells, pooled-versus-dedicated q95 wall differences were within about 0.5% and occupancy differences within about 0.2%; under symmetric side marginals this screen provides no material evidence that shared pooling beats dedicated b+b pools.

interpretation: A cross-regime synthetic knee appears near b=32,W=128: relative to the b16,W128 pair-tied baseline it cut conversation q95 wall about 13.1% for about +9.6% full-obligation occupancy, and code+straggler wall about 4.0% for about +1.6% occupancy.

Increasing W from 128 to 256 at b=32 bought only about another 5-6% q95 wall reduction while increasing q95 full-obligation occupancy about 45-48%. This is a strong tested warning against unbounded speculation when compute occupancy matters.

Side-level reuse and side-pool sharing are not the dominant heavy-tail lever. In the code+straggler regime, most remaining delay is consistent with fixed reveal-order head-of-line blocking rather than tied-slot idleness.

Peak concurrency is not captured by occupancy. b=32 needs up to 64 simultaneous side slots versus 32 at b=16, so the apparent b32 knee can be unacceptable when reserved-slot scarcity or queue interference is expensive.
No-decision deadlines remain validity-safe under the same fixed-reveal null: lowering unresolved probability is a systems gain, not a change to the statistical error budget.
scope_guards: Grid estimates are coarser than the predecessor high-precision b16/W128 paired comparison and should be used for topology screening, not exact deployment sizing.
No production speed claim; latency is normalized synthetic stress.
Symmetric candidate/incumbent latency marginals were used. The pooled-versus-dedicated near-tie can change under asymmetric models or heterogeneous hardware.
The tested candidate action sequence is one globally-certified frontier witness, not the entire 246729-multiset scheduler/policy product space.
Peak slot reservation, queue interference, cancellation latency, and monetary price are not included in q95 occupancy.

frontier.action: Add asymmetric candidate/incumbent latency and unequal side capacities. Solve b_candidate+b_incumbent fixed-budget allocation, because shared pooling was neutral only under symmetric marginals.

Treat fixed reveal head-of-line as the main heavy-tail bottleneck. Evaluate only validity-preserving straggler controls: prelaunch latency covariates, semantics-preserving deterministic replication, or deadline/no-decision; do not consume completion order statistically.
Add peak reserved-slot/queue-interference price to the objective and recompute the b16 versus b32 choice; q95 occupancy alone understates the cost of doubled concurrency.
Repeat the scheduler grid on additional globally-certified action-frontier witnesses to test whether the b32,W128 knee is policy-specific.

exact_next_action: Construct an asymmetric side-latency stress with fixed total side capacity 32 and 64. Compare equal dedicated allocation, optimized unequal candidate/incumbent allocation, and shared pooling under precommitted reveal; quantify when pooling begins to beat dedicated pools and whether heavy-tail head-of-line remains dominant.
